wa_the_perfect_crime_with_variations.notes: 36m. Steep rock with an undercut start into an open book; multiple line choices (featured face, crack/arete, or corner) lead to a quality crack with a medium-cam anchor.
25m. Awkward flared groove leads left to a yellowish flake, then a wide crack to a ledge with two big gnarled trees that make solid anchors.
~25m. Climbs right of the gnarled trees, rambling to a minor bowl with an excellent tree anchor below the notable spiral tree landmark.
60m+. Hand-crack dihedral through a blocky section past the spiral tree, or alternatively an obtuse shaft with spaced protection to a small ledge belay.
60m. Multiple options off a huge ledge; described line follows an orange coffin flake and a quality crack system into a steep, fun chimney.
60m+. Easy slab climbing trending left toward the summit with short boulder problems; may require simul-climbing with limited anchor material near the east summit edge.

wa_western_dihedral.notes: Start from a ledge with a belay bolt, reached by following the far western wall right past two tree branches. Follow a left-facing edge with face moves past two grassy ledges, each with a bolt, then walk up an angled dike to another bolt (5.8). Alternating smears and ledges lead to the anchor.

Go around the bush on its left and up a trough with sparse gear to a short wall capped by a vertical 2-inch crack. Pull onto a left-rising ramp, pass flakes to a face bolt, and climb the Predihedral on finger edges and stems to a bolt. Cross left on a sloping wave into the big red dihedral and climb its 4-inch-plus cracks to a ledge on the left. Rope drag zigzags here unless extended.

Lower back into the dihedral, pad up to the first bolt, and smear up to a delicate finger traverse rightward across the wall. Climb a couple of cracks for gear until a bolt appears to the right, cross a dirty hump rightward, then finish on clean smearing past two bolts to the anchor.
Lower-angle slab: ramble straight up for about 40 m, then look right for a single bolt that leads to the anchor.

Aim for the large Headwall Block above, following shallow troughs and slabs with at least one usable pocket for gear. At the block, a flat vertical wall, scramble left around it; blocks and ledges lead to the summit, where the belay is a sling threaded around a rock pinch. Descend by rappelling the route with two ropes.
